name: Are service continuity plans developed and documented for assets required for delivery of the critical service? (Information)
description:
SCM:G1.Q1: Are service continuity plans developed and documented for assets required for delivery of the critical service?

SCM:G1.Q1-I: Information

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if service continuity plans are developed and documented for assets required for the delivery of the critical service.
- A service continuity plan is a proactive plan of action an organization will take if a service disruption occurs.

- Plans should be developed at the time of service development and implementation.

- Plans should also be adjusted on an ongoing basis as new risks are encountered and the operational environment changes.

- Service continuity plans may require one or more sub plans such as a recovery or restoration plan.
Typical work products include:

- service continuity plan templates

- service continuity plans (including a list of relevant stakeholders)
Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization has developed and documented service continuity plans for all assets required for the delivery of the critical service.
Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Service continuity plans have been developed and documented for some assets.

- Or; service continuity plans are in development and partially documented.

Family: Service Continuity Management (SCM) > Goal 1 - Service continuity plans for high-value services are developed..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Does the organization review and update the following at least once each year: IM information management plan, media relations policy, information disclosure policy, information classification schema…
description:
AN:GV-1.Q19: Does the organization review and update the following at least once each year: IM information management plan, media relations policy, information disclosure policy, information classification schema, data retention plan, and acceptable use policy?

Guidance: Importance: Organizational plans should be reviewed at a minimum annually to ensure they are kept current.

Question Intent: This question determines whether organizational plans and policies pertaining to incident management are reviewed at least once a year to identify and implement updates.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization reviews all of its policies and plans pertaining to incident management at least once a year to identify and implement updates.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization reviews some of its policies and plans pertaining to incident management at least once a year to identify and implement updates.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

- Document review history or correspondence that substantiates review activities have occurred at least yearly for organizational incident management plans and policies.

Reference to standards/source assessments

- IMCA: 1.2.2.12 Quality.

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: PS-7, PM-1, PM-2

Tier: Intermediate.

References: SP 800-53 R5 PM-1; SP 800-53 R5 PM-2; SP 800-53 R5 PS-7.

Family: Anticipate > Governance > Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities are coordinated and aligned with internal roles and external partners.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are external dependencies prioritized?
description:
EDM:G1.Q3: Are external dependencies prioritized?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if external dependencies are prioritized. The intent of prioritization is to ensure that the organization properly directs its resources to the external dependencies that most directly impact the critical service.

Prioritization criteria may include dependencies that:

- directly affect the operation and delivery of the critical service

- support, maintain, or have custodial care of critical service assets

- support the continuity of operations of the critical service

- have access to highly sensitive or classified information

- support more than one critical service

- supply assets that support the operation of a critical service

- impact the recovery time objective of the critical service

Typical work products include:

- criteria for prioritizing external dependencies

- prioritized list of external dependencies

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization has a prioritized list of all external dependencies that support the critical service.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- The organization has prioritized some external dependencies.

References: SP 800-39; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.BE-4; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.SC-2.

CERT-RMM Reference
[EXD:SG1.SP2] Apply the prioritization criteria to the list of external dependencies to produce a prioritized list. Depending on the prioritization scheme developed by the organization, the result might be several lists, tiers, or sets of external dependencies. Be sure that external dependencies that are required for the successful execution of security activities, service continuity plans, and service restoration plans are prioritized appropriately.

Family: External Dependencies Management (EDM) > Goal 1 - External dependencies are identified and prioritized to ensure sustained operation of high-value services..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: How often does the organization test business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities that support the critical service?
description:
WI:IP-10.Q2: How often does the organization test business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities that support the critical service?

Guidance: Importance: Business continuity and DR capabilities require frequent testing to confirm that systems function properly and that staff thoroughly understand their roles. Untested systems cannot be fully relied upon.

Question Intent: To determine if the organization tests its business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities on a regular basis. The service continuity test schedule should meet the requirements of the mission critical service.

- The tests should establish the viability, accuracy, and completeness of the plan.

- The tests should also provide information about the organization’s level of preparedness.

- The tests are performed under conditions established by the organization, and the results of the test should be recorded and documented.

- Methods for testing contingency plans to determine the effectiveness of the plans and identify potential weaknesses include checklists, walk-through and tabletop exercises, simulations (parallel or full interrupt), and comprehensive exercises.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- All business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities are tested at least annually.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- All business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities activities are tested at a frequency of greater than once a year but at least every 2 years.

- Or, some business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities are tested at least annually.

Possible evidence

- Documented test results

Reference to standards/source assessments

- Cyber IST: Q.25.1

Tier: Basic.

Detail options (select all that apply): More than once a year; Annually; Every two years; The organization does not test business continuity and disaster recovery capabilities

References: SP 800-53 R5 CP-4; SP 800-53 R5 IR-3; SP 800-53 R5 PM-14.

Family: Withstand > Information Protection > Response and recovery plans are tested.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Have risk management activities standards and guidelines been identified and implemented?
description:
RM:MIL2.Q4: Have risk management activities standards and guidelines been identified and implemented?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if standards and guidelines for performing risk management activities have been implemented.

- Standards establish expectations for performance.

- Guidelines are issued by an organization to ensure the performance of risk management activities meets standards and is predictable, measurable, and repeatable.

Standards and guidelines typically address:

- identifying risk sources and categories of risk

- defining risk parameters (such as risk tolerance thresholds) and risk measurement criteria

- assigning risk priorities based on risk analysis

- assigning risk dispositions

- developing risk mitigation plans

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization has implemented documented standards and guidelines for performing risk management activities.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Some standards and guidelines have been implemented.

References: Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.RM-1.

CERT-RMM Reference
Consider developing standards and guidelines that address:

- identifying risk sources and categories of risk

- defining risk parameters (such as risk tolerance thresholds) and risk measurement criteria

- assigning risk priorities based on risk valuation

- assigning risk dispositions

- developing risk mitigation plans

Family: Risk Management (RM) > MIL2 - Planned.

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are the assets that directly support the critical service inventoried (technology includes hardware, software, and external information systems)? (Facilities)
description:
AM:G2.Q1: Are the assets that directly support the critical service inventoried (technology includes hardware, software, and external information systems)?

AM:G2.Q1-F: Facilities

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if the assets that support the critical service are inventoried.

- The organization should inventory the assets (people, information, technology, and facilities) required for the delivery of the critical service.

- Inventories of assets may exist in multiple forms or physical locations.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization inventories all assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- The organization inventories some assets.

CERT-RMM Reference [ADM:SG1.SP1] Identify and inventory high-value assets. An organization must be able to identify its high-value assets, document them, and establish their value in order to develop strategies for protecting and sustaining assets commensurate with their value to services.

Additional References:
- Special Publication 800-18 Revision 1 "Guide for Developing Security Plans for Federal Information Systems", Page 2-3

- NIST CSF References: ID.AM, ID.AM-1,ID.AM-2, ID.AM-4

Family: Asset Management (AM) > Goal 2 - Assets are inventoried, and the authority and responsibility for these assets is established..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Policies and procedures for hiring/terminating processes on employees, contractors, or support companies to include background checks and contract agreements approved and implemented
description:
PS-1: Policies and procedures for hiring/terminating processes on employees, contractors, or support companies to include background checks and contract agreements approved and implemented.

Guidance: A background check on employees is required before they may be given access to the PCS system.

References: AWWA Risk Management Guidance PS-1.

Family: Governance and Risk Management.

Source: AWWA Cybersecurity Guidance v4.0, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Does the acquirer evaluate technology assets that support the critical service for vulnerabilities before they are acquired?
description:
RF:G6.Q2: Does the acquirer evaluate technology assets that support the critical service for vulnerabilities before they are acquired?

Guidance: Question intent: To determine if the acquirer has a process to evaluate technology assets for vulnerabilities prior to completing the acquisition of these assets.
This practice is important because it helps the acquirer obtain technology that is more likely to satisfy the requirements and importance of the critical service.
An affirmative answer to this question requires that the acquirer has some process or have assigned responsibility to staff to become aware of vulnerabilities to technology that the acquirer intends to purchase to support the critical service. In practice, the acquirer's ability to gather effective, complete vulnerability information may vary substantially depending on the specific technology item.
Some ways that the acquirer can evaluate technology vulnerabilities before acquisition include

- incorporating vulnerability-reporting requirements in formal technology purchase agreements

- participating in ICS-CERT or other organizations to become aware of vulnerabilities

- reviewing system configurations for potential vulnerabilities

- communicating with peer acquirers that also use particular external entities

- researching vulnerability information in publicly available databases and sources
Typical work products:

- vulnerability reports

- assignment of responsibility in job descriptions

- internal correspondence
Criteria for "Yes" Response:

- The acquirer evaluates all technology assets to support the critical service for vulnerabilities before acquiring and deploying these assets internally.

Criteria for "Incomplete" Response:

- The acquirer evaluates some technology assets for vulnerabilities before acquiring them, or this practice appears otherwise incomplete.

References: EDM Question Set with Guidance; EDM | NIST Cyber Security Framework Crosswalks.

CERT-RMM References

[VAR: SG2.SP2] Discover vulnerabilities

Data collection should be coordinated to discover vulnerabilities and populate the vulnerability repository as efficiently as possible.

[VAR: SG3.SP1] Manage Exposure to Vulnerabilities

Develop a vulnerability management strategy for all vulnerabilities that require resolution. The strategy should address the actions that the organization will take to reduce or eliminate exposure or to provide an operational workaround if preferable. This includes ensuring that relevant stakeholders are informed of resolution activities.

Additional References

NIST Special Publication 800-53 Revision 4 , “Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations”, SA-12(2) Supply Chain Protection | Supplier Reviews.

The organization conducts a supplier review prior to entering into a contractual agreement to acquire the information system, system component, or information system service .

Supplemental Guidance : Supplier reviews include, for example: (i) analysis of supplier processes used to design, develop, test, implement, verify, deliver, and support information systems, system components, and information system services; and (ii) assessment of supplier training and experience in developing systems, components, or services with the required security capability. These reviews provide organizations with increased levels of visibility into supplier activities during the system development life cycle to promote more effective supply chain risk management. Supplier reviews can also help to determine whether primary suppliers have security safeguards in place and a practice for vetting subordinate suppliers, for example, second- and third-tier suppliers, and any subcontractors.

Protection of organizational information systems is accomplished through threat awareness, by the identification, management, and reduction of vulnerabilities at each phase of the life cycle and the use of complementary, mutually reinforcing strategies to respond to risk. Organizations consider implementing a standardized process to address supply chain risk with respect to information systems and system components, and to educate the acquisition workforce on threats, risk, and required security controls.

NIST Special Publication 800-40 Version 3.0 , “Creating a Patch Management and Vulnerability Management Program.” 2.3.2 Monitoring Vulnerabilities, Remediations, and Threats, 7.

Vendors are the authoritative source of information for patches related to their products. However, many vendors will not announce vulnerabilities in their products until patches are available; accordingly, monitoring third-party vulnerability resources as well is recommended .

ISO 27036-3 , “Information technology - Security techniques - Information Security for Supplier Relationships” Part 3, 6.

NIST CSF References: ID.BE-4, ID.RA-1

Family: Relationship Formation - MIL-1 > Goal 6 – Technology asset supply chain risks are managed..

Source: CISA EDM, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Does the organization establish criteria that define which assets are mission critical?
description:
WI:AM-1.Q7: Does the organization establish criteria that define which assets are mission critical?

Guidance: Importance: If everything is important, then nothing is important. Establishing criteria on how to define “critical” will help ensure that only truly important systems are included in the critical listing.

Question Intent: To determine if organizations have defined criteria to designate which systems and data are mission critical.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- Documented criteria exist to define systems and data as mission critical.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- Documented criteria are being developed to define systems and data as mission critical.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

- Up-to-date list or database of critical systems and data

- Up-to-date list of POCs for critical systems and data

- Procedures for designating systems and data as critical

Reference to standards/source assessments

- IMCA: 1.2.3.01

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: RA-9, CM-8, PM-5

Tier: Basic.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CM-8; SP 800-53 R5 PM-5; SP 800-53 R5 RA-9.

Family: Withstand > Asset Management > Physical devices and systems within the organization are inventoried.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are service continuity plans developed and documented for assets required for delivery of the critical service?
description:
SCM:G1.Q1: Are service continuity plans developed and documented for assets required for delivery of the critical service?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if service continuity plans are developed and documented for assets required for the delivery of the critical service.

- A service continuity plan is a proactive plan of action an organization will take if a service disruption occurs.

- Plans should be developed at the time of service development and implementation.

- Plans should also be adjusted on an ongoing basis as new risks are encountered and the operational environment changes.

- Service continuity plans may require one or more sub plans such as a recovery or restoration plan.

Typical work products include:

- service continuity plan templates

- service continuity plans (including a list of relevant stakeholders)

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization has developed and documented service continuity plans for all assets required for the delivery of the critical service.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Service continuity plans have been developed and documented for some assets.

- Or; service continuity plans are in development and partially documented.

References: SP 800-34 R1 Page A.3-1; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.SC-5; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.IP-9.

CERT-RMM Reference
[SC:SG3.SP2] Document the service continuity plans using available templates as appropriate. A service continuity plan typically includes the following information:
- identification of authority for initiating and executing the plan (plan ownership)

- identification of the communication mechanism to initiate execution of the plan

Family: Service Continuity Management (SCM) > Goal 1 - Service continuity plans for high-value services are developed..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Is the audit log repository protected from unauthorized modification or deletion?
description:
WI:AE-3.Q4: Is the audit log repository protected from unauthorized modification or deletion?

Guidance: Importance: Protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of audit log information . Providing access to a repository via common mechanism can increase the susceptibility of data and information to unauthorized access, disclosure, use, deletion, or modification and can adversely affect the inherent capability provided by the repository.

Question Intent: To determine if repositories are protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization has implemented protections against the unauthorized modification or deletion of audit log data.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization is in the process of implementing protections against the unauthorized modification or deletion of audit log data.

Possible evidence

- SIEM configuration

- Backup solution configuration

- Backup file system access control lists

Reference to standards/source assessments

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-6, CA-7, IR-4, IR-5, IR-8, SI-4

Tier: Intermediate.

Family: Withstand > Anomalies and Events > Event data are collected and correlated from multiple sources and sensors.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are events analyzed to determine if they are related to other events?
description:
IM:G2.Q4: Are events analyzed to determine if they are related to other events?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if events are analyzed for their relationship to other events.

- Analysis should be conducted to determine whether the event correlates to other events (correlation may indicate larger issues, problems, or incidents).

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization analyzes all events relevant to the critical service to determine if they are related to other events.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- The organization analyzes some events.

References: Handbook for (CSIRTs); SP 800-61 R2 Section 3.4; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 DE.AE-2; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 DE.AE-3.

CERT-RMM Reference [IMC:SG2.SP4] Perform correlation analysis on event reports to determine if there is affinity between two or more events.

Family: Incident Management (IM) > Goal 2 - A process for detecting, reporting, triaging, and analyzing events is established..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Is there a standard set of tools and/or methods in use to detect unauthorized mobile code in assets?
description:
WI:CM-5.Q1: Is there a standard set of tools and/or methods in use to detect unauthorized mobile code in assets?

Guidance: Importance: Organizations must continuously monitor their systems and related networks to prevent the intrusion of threat actors and avoid the injection of malicious code. Scanning enables and organization to monitor for malicious code injection and avoid significant breach.

Question Intent: The question tries to determine the malicious code scanning practices of the organization as it relates to continuous monitoring practices.

Mobile code technologies include Java, JavaScript, ActiveX, Postscript, PDF, Flash animations, and VBScript. Decisions regarding the use of mobile code in organizational systems are based on the potential for the code to cause damage to the systems if used maliciously. Usage restrictions and implementation guidance apply to the selection and use of mobile code installed on servers and mobile code downloaded and executed on individual workstations, notebook computers, and devices (e.g., smart phones). Mobile code policy and procedures address controlling or preventing the development, acquisition, or introduction of unacceptable mobile code in systems, including requiring mobile code to be digitally signed by a trusted source.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization has and properly utilizes tools to conduct regular scanning for vulnerabilities within its mobile code. Policy and procedure exist to guide the workforce in appropriate scanning practices. Documentation or logs reflect those scans are conducted in a timely fashion. Tools are updated on a periodic basis to ensure that new vulnerabilities are detected before risks may come to fruition.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization has the proper tools and policies that enable mobile code technology scanning. However, the organization may fail to properly configure the tools or update them with any regular periodicity. Scans may take place, but the organization fails to prioritize and act upon necessary patching.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

- Organizational policies and procedures that direct the proper use of scanning tools

- Documentation or logs that indicate scanning activities

- Scanning activity results along with evidence of disposition and risk-based decisions to patch vulnerabilities

Reference to standards/source assessments

- CRR VM:G1.Q4, 800-171 R2, 3.13.13, NIST 800-53: SC-18, SI-4, SC-44.

Tier: Basic.

References: SP 800-53 R5 SC-18; SP 800-53 R5 SC-18(1); SP 800-53 R5 SC-44; SP 800-53 R5 SI-4.

Family: Withstand > Security Continuous Monitoring > Unauthorized mobile code is detected.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Is there a process to ensure event evidence is handled as required by law or other obligations?
description:
AN:GV-3.Q4: Is there a process to ensure event evidence is handled as required by law or other obligations?

Guidance: Importance: Failure to comply with statutory requirements for evidence handling can result in legal ramifications. Therefore, it is critical that organizations abide by the industry-specific, national, regional, and state regulations for the areas in which the organization operates.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has implemented a process to ensure event evidence is handled as required by law or other obligations.

Based on applicable requirements the organization should develop a process using standards and guidelines for the collection, documentation, and preservation of event evidence.

Staff should be trained on the organizational process for proper identification and handling of evidence to ensure that the evidence is not altered, and that integrity is maintained.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- There is a documented process to ensure event evidence is handled as required by law or other obligations.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- A process is in development and partially documented.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

- Incident response plan, Standard Operating Procedure for Incident Management, or Other relevant organizational policy covering incident management.

Reference to standards/source assessments

- CRR: IM:G2.Q9

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-1, IR-8(1), AU-10

Tier: Intermediate.

References: SP 800-53 R5 AU-10; SP 800-53 R5 IR-1; SP 800-53 R5 IR-8(1).

Family: Anticipate > Governance > Legal and regulatory requirements regarding cybersecurity, including privacy and civil liberties obligations, are understood and managed.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Implement Cybersecurity Training
description:
Goal 3.J: Implement Cybersecurity Training

Outcome: Organizational users learn and perform more secure behaviors.

Scope: All employees, contractors, partners, suppliers, providers, and other users of the organization's non-public resources.

Risk addressed: Train users on recognizing access or manipulation attempts by adversaries to lower the risk of successful spear phishing, social engineering, and other techniques that involve user interaction.

Recommended action: New employees receive initial cybersecurity training prior to accessing computer systems.

Provide at least annual cybersecurity training for all organizational users to train personnel in recognizing social engineering attempts and other common attacks, reporting attacks and suspicious activity, complying with acceptable use policies, and performing basic cyber hygiene tasks (e.g., choosing passwords, protecting credentials).

Identify the specialized roles within the organization that require additional cybersecurity training, such as physical and cybersecurity personnel, system administrators, finance personnel, senior leadership, and anyone with access to business-critical data. Provide role-based cybersecurity training to all those in specialized roles, including contractors, partners, suppliers, and other third parties.

OT: Personnel should receive security awareness and training for the OT environment. In addition, organizations should identify, document, and train all personnel who have significant OT roles and responsibilities.

Cost 1 of 3, impact high, complexity moderate.

Free CISA services: CISA Training
Cybersecurity Training & Exercises

References: SP 800-53 R5 AT-2; NIST SP 800-82r3 AT-2; SP 800-53 R5 AT-3; NIST SP 800-82r3 AT-3; The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 PR.AT-01; The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 PR.AT-02.

Family: Protect.

Source: CISA CPG 2.0, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are all relevant elements of the organization involved in testing the incident detection, handling, and response processes?
description:
PI:G2.Q5: Are all relevant elements of the organization involved in testing the incident detection, handling, and response processes?

Guidance: Question Intent: To determine if all relevant elements of the organization are involved in testing the incident detection, handling and response process, procedures and activities.

- All relevant stakeholders, both internal and external, should be identified and involved in testing the incident detection, handling, and response processes, procedures and activities.

- The level of involvement and commitment of stakeholders in the testing of the plan should be established.

- Methods of communicating with all relevant stakeholders should be established.

- All relevant stakeholders should understand and accept their roles and responsibilities.

Typical work products include :

- Documented Incident detection, handling, and response processes, procedures, and activities that include relevant stakeholders.

- Documented Incident detection, handling, and response test plans that include relevant stakeholders.

- Documented test report that show all relevant participating stakeholders.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- All relevant elements (stakeholders) of the organization are involved in testing the Incident detection, handling, and response processes, procedures and activities.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Some relevant elements (stakeholders) of the organization are involved in testing.

References: SP 800-84 2; SP 800-61 R2 2.3.3; IMR | NIST Cyber Security Framework Crosswalks; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.SC-5; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.IP-10.

CERT-RMM Reference V1.2

[SC:SG5.SP2] Develop and Document Test Plans
The incident response test plan should identify all internal and external stakeholders involved in the testing exercise, and their roles and expected participation. The organization should ensure that all relevant stakeholders are involved in the planned testing.

Family: Post-Incident Analysis and Testing (PI) > Goal 2 - The incident detection, handling, and response capability is tested and exercised..

Source: CISA IMR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are integrity requirements used to determine which staff members are authorized to modify event and incident information?
description:
PS:G2.Q4: Are integrity requirements used to determine which staff members are authorized to modify event and incident information?

Guidance: Question Intent: To determine if integrity requirements of event and incident information assets are used to determine which staff members are authorized to modify those assets.

- Integrity requirements address qualifications to ensure the information is :

- complete and intact

- accurate and valid

- authorized and official

- Integrity requirements are a specific form of protection requirement.

- Controlling which staff members are authorized to modify information assets helps ensure the continued integrity of those assets. Role-based access is a method of defining and implementing this form of integrity re-equipment.

- A fundamental way of controlling modifications to information assets is to limit access to those assets, both:

- electronically (by controlling access to networks, servers, application systems, and databases and files); and

- physically (by limiting access to file rooms, work areas, computer rooms, and facilities)

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The integrity requirements for all event and incident information assets are used to determine which staff members are authorized to modify those assets.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- The integrity requirements for some event and incident information assets are used to determine which staff members are authorized to modify those assets.

References: SP 800-53A R4 AC-2; IMR | NIST Cyber Security Framework Crosswalks; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AC-4; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.IP-11; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.IP-3.

CERT-RMM Reference V1.2

[KIM:SG5.SP1] Control Modification of Information Assets
Identify and document staff who are authorized to modify information assets, relative to the asset's integrity requirements. This information may be specifically included as part of the information asset's resilience requirements.

Family: Protect and Sustain the Incident Management Function (PS) > Goal 2 - The confidentiality, integrity and availability of event and incident information is managed..

Source: CISA IMR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Centralized authentication system or single sign-on established to authorize access from a central system
description:
SC-2: Centralized authentication system or single sign-on established to authorize access from a central system.

Guidance: Operators have one username and password for PCS equipment which is managed from a central system.

References: AWWA Risk Management Guidance SC-2.

Family: Access Control.

Source: AWWA Cybersecurity Guidance v4.0, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are risks related to the performance of planned controls management activities identified, analyzed, disposed of, monitored, and controlled?
description:
CM:MIL3.Q4: Are risks related to the performance of planned controls management activities identified, analyzed, disposed of, monitored, and controlled?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if the organization identifies, analyzes, and mitigates risks related to the performance of the controls management activities.

- The intent is to determine risks that prevent the organization from performing controls management activities (controls management process), not the risks to the organization if the activities are not performed.

Risks to consider in relation to the controls management process include:

- poorly defined controls management processes

- inadequate staffing

- inadequate funding

- unqualified staff

- lack of tools

- lack of a documented plan, policy, standards, and guidelines

- lack of stakeholder involvement

- lack of management oversight

Criteria for “Yes” Response

- Risks to the performance of all planned controls management activities are identified, analyzed, disposed of, monitored, and controlled.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Risks to the performance of some of the planned controls management activities are identified, analyzed, disposed of, monitored, and controlled.

- Or; risks to the performance of planned controls management activities are identified, but are not analyzed, disposed of, monitored, or controlled.

References: Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.GV-4; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.RA-6.

CERT-RMM Reference Consider ensuring that risk arising from the failure of controls management is identified, assessed, and mitigated.

Family: Controls Management (CM) > MIL3 - Managed.

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Does the organization plan for the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity?
description:
AN:CP-3.Q1: Does the organization plan for the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity?

Guidance: Importance: Business continuity planning is critical to minimize losses.

Question Intent: This question determines if the organization has a business continuity plan in place to provide the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity.

- Business continuity planning requires organizations to perform business process analyses (BPAs), business impact analyses (BIAs), and risk assessments. These need to be performed to identify essential mission and business functions that require minimal or no loss of operation, so they can then be prioritized when planning for business continuity capabilities.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization has a fully documented and developed business continuity function that provides for the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization has a partially documented and developed business continuity function that provides for the continuance of essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

- Business continuity plan, business process analyses (BPAs), business impact analyses (BIAs), risk assessments

Reference to standards/source assessments

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-2(5)

Tier: Advanced.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CP-2(5).

Family: Anticipate > Coordinated Protection > Orchestration.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Does the organization disrupt and adversely affect the system or system component to validate the effectiveness of protections?
description:
AN:CP-4.Q7: Does the organization disrupt and adversely affect the system or system component to validate the effectiveness of protections?

Guidance: Importance: The quality of penetration testing engagements can vary; therefore, organizations should specify the level of rigor and scope of such tests to accurately model the types of attacks they are likely to face as an organization.

Question Intent: This question seeks to determine if the organization holds penetration testing exercises to quality standards such as rigor and organization-defined constraints.

Penetration tests should incorporate adversary emulation techniques, use pre-determined levels of rigor, and consider any organization-defined constraints that may limit the scope of the testing

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization requires the developers of systems, system components, or system services to perform penetration testing and specifies a given level of rigor (breadth and depth) as well as any additional organization-defined constraints that the penetration test must follow.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization requires the developers of systems, system components, or system services to perform penetration testing, however the organization does not specify a given level of rigor (breadth and depth) or organization-defined constraints for the penetration testing.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

- Rules of engagement for a penetration test performed against the system, system component, or system service that includes description of the level of rigor used, as well as the constraints the penetration testers had to work under.

Reference to standards/source assessments

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-9(1)

Tier: Advanced.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CP-9(1).

Family: Anticipate > Coordinated Protection > Self-Challenge.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Is a repository used for recording information about vulnerabilities and their resolution?
description:
RE:AN-5.Q6: Is a repository used for recording information about vulnerabilities and their resolution?

Guidance: Importance: A vulnerability repository as the central source of vulnerability life-cycle information is an essential construct that is vital to the efficiency and effectiveness of other operational resilience management processes.

Question Intent: To determine if a repository for recording information about vulnerabilities and their resolution is used.

- a vulnerability repository should be used as the central source of vulnerability lifecycle information.

- a vulnerability repository supports analysis, disposition, trending, root cause analysis, and vulnerability management Information that should be recorded includes:

- a unique identifier

- description of the vulnerability

- date entered into the repository

- references to the source of the vulnerability

- the priority of the vulnerability (high, medium, low)

- categorization and disposition of the vulnerability

- individuals or teams assigned to analyze and remediate the vulnerability

- a log of actions taken to reduce or eliminate the vulnerability

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization uses a repository to record all vulnerability information for all the assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization uses a repository to record some vulnerability information; Or;

- the organization uses a repository to record all vulnerability information for some assets.

Possible evidence

- Vulnerability repository

- Vulnerability data and information

Reference to standards/source assessments

- CRR: VM:G2.Q6.

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: SI-5, PM-15

Tier: Basic.

References: SP 800-53 R5 RA-5.

Family: Recover > Analysis > Processes are established to receive, analyze and respond to vulnerabilities disclosed to the organization from internal and external sources (e.g. internal testing, security bulletins, or security researchers).

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Have qualified staff been assigned to perform incident management activities as planned?
description:
IM:MIL3.Q2: Have qualified staff been assigned to perform incident management activities as planned?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if qualified staff have been assigned. The intent of this question is to evaluate the qualifications of the staff, not the completeness of the plan.

- Qualified means that staff are appropriately skilled to perform incident management activities.

Examples of staff include personnel responsible for:

- detecting, logging, analyzing, reporting, and tracking events

- collecting and preserving evidence

- declaring an incident from one or more events

- managing incidents and making critical decisions

- analyzing and responding to incidents, including escalation procedures

- communicating incidents

- performing post-incident reviews, resolving problems, and closing incidents

- creating and maintaining the incident knowledge base

- managing external entities that have contractual obligations for process activities

Examples of skills needed include:

- event detection, reporting, and tracking, including service desk activities

- documenting and logging event reports

- collecting and preserving evidence

- declaring incidents

- incident analysis

- escalating and communicating incidents

- understanding and applying laws, rules, and regulations

- performing root-cause analysis and post-incident review

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- All staff assigned to perform the planned incident management activities are appropriately skilled.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Some staff assigned have the skill necessary to perform their roles.

References: Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AT.

CERT-RMM Reference
Consider ensuring that responsible staff are trained in skills required in the incident management process. Examples of these skills include:

- event detection, reporting, and tracking, including service desk activities

- documenting and logging event reports

- collecting and preserving evidence

- technical analysis of events and incidents, including triage

- declaring incidents

- escalating and communicating incidents

- understanding and applying laws, rules, and regulations

- performing incident response, including damage containment

- creating, managing, and deploying incident response teams

- developing and implementing administrative, technical, and physical controls

- performing root-cause analysis and post-incident review

- using tools, techniques, and methods necessary to handle incidents throughout their life cycle, including those necessary to perform the process using the selected methods, techniques, and tools

- knowledge unique to each type of asset or service that may be the target of an incident

- working effectively and collaborating with asset owners and custodians

- eliciting and prioritizing stakeholder requirements and needs and interpreting them to develop effective incident management plans and plans for handling specific types of incidents

Family: Incident Management (IM) > MIL3 - Managed.

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Does the organization coordinate cybersecurity activities across system, mission, and organizational levels?
description:
AN:CP-2.Q1: Does the organization coordinate cybersecurity activities across system, mission, and organizational levels?

Guidance: Importance: The implementation of an organization’s cybersecurity strategy will vary depending on the business units responsible for its execution, therefore it is useful to consider how it is operationalized in different contexts across the organization.

Question Intent: This question is seeking to learn more about how the organization coordinates cybersecurity activities across systems, missions, and organization levels.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The respondent is confident in their response, demonstrates clear knowledge of cybersecurity activities across the organization, and provides an example of how activities are implemented at each level.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The respondent is timid in their answer; However, they provide a brief response as to how cybersecurity activities are embedded in the organization’s business practices. More information could be provided on specific implementation with regards to the system, mission, and organization levels.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible Evidence

- Organizational cybersecurity or information security strategy.

Reference to standards/source assessments

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IA-1, PM-1, CP-4(1)

- NIST 800-160, Rev. 1

Tier: Advanced.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CP-4(1); SP 800-53 R5 IA-1; SP 800-53 R5 PM-1.

Family: Anticipate > Coordinated Protection > Consistency Analysis.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are external dependencies prioritized?
description:
AN:BE-4.Q5: Are external dependencies prioritized?

Guidance: Importance: Prioritization is important to ensure that resilience resources are directed where they best support the mission.

Question Intent: Determine if external dependencies are prioritized. External dependencies can include IT infrastructure providers, software-as-a-service providers, utilities, or data or voice service providers, to name just a few.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- Criteria for prioritizing external dependencies and prioritized list of external dependencies.

Criteria for Partial Response:

- Having only partial list of external dependencies with no criteria for prioritization.

Possible Evidence

- Criteria for prioritizing external dependencies and prioritized list of external dependencies.

Reference to standards/source assessments

- CRR: EDM:G1.Q3

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-8(1), RA-9, PE-9, PE-11, PM-8

Tier: Intermediate.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CP-8(1); SP 800-53 R5 PE-11; SP 800-53 R5 PE-9; SP 800-53 R5 PM-8; SP 800-53 R5 RA-9.

Family: Anticipate > Business Environment > Dependencies and critical functions for delivery of critical services are established.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are unauthorized or unexplained modifications to technology assets addressed?
description:
WI:IP-3.Q8: Are unauthorized or unexplained modifications to technology assets addressed?

Guidance: Importance: Unauthorized or unexplained modifications to assets can indicate the presence of an attacker or of ad hoc changes that have not been vetted through the change management process. Either way, they represent a significant risk to resilience and should be investigated.

Question Intent: To determine if unauthorized or unexplained modifications to technology assets are addressed.

- Periodically verify (through monitoring and auditing) that changes to configurations are valid and authorized.

- Identify action items that are required to repair any unauthorized or unexplained modifications to technology assets.

- Track action items to closure.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- All unauthorized or unexplained modifications to technology assets that support the critical service are addressed.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- Some unauthorized or unexplained modifications to technology assets are addressed.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

- Documentation showing how unauthorized or unexplained modifications are addressed

- IT or OT service desk tickets showing response to unexplained modifications

- Incident response tickets/documentation showing review of unexplained modifications

Reference to standards/source assessments

- CRR CCM:G2.Q6

Tier: Intermediate.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CM-3; SP 800-53 R5 CM-4; SP 800-53 R5 SA-10.

Family: Withstand > Information Protection > Configuration change control processes are in place.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Establish Incident Communication Procedures
description:
Goal 5.A: Establish Incident Communication Procedures

Outcome: Coordinate crisis communication methods between internal and external organization partners and critical suppliers.

Scope: Organization-wide.

Risk addressed: Without established communication procedures, incidents can disrupt coordination among response teams, slowing incident resolution, increasing downtime, and amplifying overall damage.

Recommended action: Design a communications plan that identifies stakeholders and mechanisms for coordination and communications during an incident.

Collaborate with stakeholders and securely share information consistent with response plans and information-sharing agreements. Priorities for sharing information include preventing the spread of infections to other systems and networks.

Regularly update senior leadership on the status of major incidents.

Notify human resources when malicious insider activity occurs.

Establish and follow media communications procedures for incident response that comply with the organization's policies on media interaction and information disclosure.

IT implementation criteria (answer Yes only when every bullet is met): - Do organizational personnel with incident reporting responsibilities, or those to whom incident information is
reported, follow established procedures for incident communication?

- Is the control in place, such that any remaining gaps are relatively minor? (
In Progress

- Is the organization actively working to implement this control, such that it is at least 10% implemented?

Scoped

- Does the organization have a plan and funding allocated to implement this goal? (i.e., at least a POA&M with
allocated funding for it?)

Not Implemented

- None of the above implementation levels are met.

OT implementation criteria (answer Yes only when every bullet is met): - Does the organization identify personnel responsible for identifying critical roles and responsibilities for
incident response? Organizations should also make sure those individuals are properly trained, licensed and
capable of performing OT incident response reporting.

Cost 1 of 3, impact high, complexity moderate.

Free CISA services: Guidance on effective communications in a cyber incident
Incident Management

References: SP 800-53 R5 IR-4; NIST SP 800-82r3 IR-4; SP 800-53 R5 IR-6; NIST SP 800-82r3 IR-6; SP 800-53 R5 IR-7; The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 RS.CO-03; SP 800-53 R5 SR-3; SP 800-53 R5 SR-8.

Family: Respond.

Source: CISA CPG 2.0, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Phishing
description:
8.S.A.3: Phishing
- Proactively block websites (URLs) referenced in “click attacks.”
- Identify malware that might have been installed on computers, and remediate appropriately if present

Guidance: Phishing
• Proactively block websites (URLs) referenced in “click attacks.”
• Identify malware that might have been installed on computers, and remediate appropriately if present

Family: Incident Response.

Source: HHS 405(d) HICP, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are employees held accountable for executing the roles and responsibilities detailed in the incident management plan?
description:
PR:G1.Q4: Are employees held accountable for executing the roles and responsibilities detailed in the incident management plan?

Guidance: Question Intent: To determine if employees are held accountable for executing the roles and responsibilities defined in the incident management plan.

- The organization should define the roles and responsibilities required to achieve the plan's objectives.

- Job descriptions are a means to ensure that incident management staff understand their roles and are aware of their responsibilities .

- Employee reviews should include assessment of their performance of incident management roles and responsibilities.

- Specific remediation actions should be taken when employees do not perform their roles and responsibilities properly.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- All employees are held accountable for executing their roles and responsibilities.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Some employees are held accountable for executing their roles and responsibilities.

- Or, employees are sometimes held accountable for executing their roles and responsibilities.

References: IMR | NIST Cyber Security Framework Crosswalks; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 DE.DP-1; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.IP-11.

CERT-RMM Reference V1.2

[IMC:SG1.SP2] Assign Staff to the Incident Management Plan
[EXD:SG1.SP1] Identify External Dependencies
Develop detailed job descriptions for each role and responsibility detailed in the incident management plan. The job description should clearly state the duties, expectations, and requirements of each role defined in the plan.

Family: Prepare for Incident Response (PR) > Goal 1 - A process to detect and analyze events, identify incidents, and determine an organizational response is established..

Source: CISA IMR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are the high-value assets (technology, information, people, and facilities) that directly support the organization’s critical services inventoried?
description:
EH:G1.Q3: Are the high-value assets (technology, information, people, and facilities) that directly support the organization’s critical services inventoried?

Guidance: Question Intent: To determine if the assets that support the organization's critical services are inventoried.

- The organization should inventory the assets (people, information, technology, and facilities) required for the delivery of its critical services .

- Inventories of assets may exist in multiple forms or physical locations.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization inventories all assets (technology, information, people and facilities) for all services designated as critical by the organization.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- The organization inventories some assets for all services designated as critical or the organization inventories all assets for some of the services designated as critical.

References: SP 800-61 R2 3.1.1; SP 800-53A R4 CA-3; SP 800-53A R4 CM-2; SP 800-53A R4 CM-8; SP 800-53A R4 CP-2(8); SP 800-18 R1; IMR | NIST Cyber Security Framework Crosswalks; SP 800-53A R4 PM-5; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM-1; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM-2; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM-3; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM-4; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.BE-4; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.BE-5.

CERT-RMM Reference V1.2
[ADM:SG1.SP1] Inventory Assets
Identify and inventory high-value assets (technology, information, people, and facilities). An organization must be able to identify its high-value assets, document them, and establish their value in order to develop strategies for protecting and sustaining assets commensurate with their value to services./p>
Consider the following attributes for each asset:

- protection and sustainment requirements

- owners and custodians

- physical Locations

- organizational communications and data flows

- critical service(s) supported

- configuration standards

- baseline of network operations associated

- baseline of expected data flows

Family: Event Detection and Handling (EH) > Goal 1 - Organizational services and assets are prioritized and supported by event detection and handling capabilities..

Source: CISA IMR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are incidents managed and tracked to resolution?
description:
RE:MI-1.Q2: Are incidents managed and tracked to resolution?

Guidance: Importance: Tracking incidents to closure provides a mechanism for the organization to know what incidents are still open and are in need further effort to resolve. This also provides an indication to all relevant stakeholders that no further actions are required or outstanding for the incident.

Question Intent: To determine if incidents are tracked and managed to resolution.

- Incidents may be open for an extended period of time, may not have followed the organization’s incident management process or may not have been formally closed.

- The organization should have a process for the formal closure of incidents that results in formally logging a status of “closed” in the incident knowledge base.

- The status of incidents in the incident knowledge base should be reviewed regularly to determine if open incidents should be closed or need additional action.

Typical work products include:

- criteria for incident closure

- incident closure reports

- updated incident knowledgebase

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization tracks and manages all incidents to resolution.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization tracks and manages some incidents to resolution.

Possible evidence

- Incident status reports or knowledgebase detailing the status of all incidents. This report should clearly designate whether the incident has been closed or is still in some form of open status.

Reference to standards/source assessments

- IMR: IR:G3.Q7

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: IR-4, IR-5, AU-6

Tier: Intermediate.

References: SP 800-53 R5 AU-6; SP 800-53 R5 IR-4; SP 800-53 R5 IR-5.

Family: Recover > Mitigation > Incidents are mitigated.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are access (including identities and credentials) requests reviewed and approved by the asset owner?
description:
AM:G5.Q2: Are access (including identities and credentials) requests reviewed and approved by the asset owner?

Guidance: Question Intent:
To determine if access requests are reviewed and approved by the asset owner.

- Asset owners are responsible for reviewing the access request and the asset's protection requirements to decide whether to approve or deny access.

- The access provided should be commensurate with and not exceed the requestor's job responsibilities.

- If the custodian of the asset is different from the owner, the owner should communicate in writing the approval for the request.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- All access requests for assets that support the critical service are reviewed and approved by the asset owner.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Some access requests for assets that support the critical service are reviewed and approved by the asset owner.

References: SP 800-53 R5 AC-1; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AC-1; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AC-2; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AC-3; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AC-6; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AC-7.

CERT-RMM Reference [AM:SG1.SP1] Access requests should be sponsored by an appropriate person in the organization (i.e., a supervisor or manager) and should be directly submitted to and approved by the owner of the assets (or their agents) to which access is being requested. Access requests should include proper justification for the request and should be approved by the sponsor of the request.

Family: Asset Management (AM) > Goal 5 - Access to assets is managed..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are users who attempt to install rogue hardware counseled against installing rogue hardware?
description:
UM:A.Q09: Are users who attempt to install rogue hardware counseled against installing rogue hardware?

Guidance: Question intent: to determine if users who attempt to install or connect rogue or unauthorized hardware to the organization’s networks are counseled against adding rogue devices to the organization’s networks.

Ensure a policy addressing the addition of unauthorized hardware to the organization’s networks is developed. The policy should, at a minimum, indicate that adding unauthorized hardware to the organization’s networks is prohibited.

The policy should also direct that awareness training be developed to train users of the issues surrounding the addition of unauthorized or rogue hardware to the organizations networks.

Possible actions:

- Develop or update security policies to ensure rogue or unauthorized hardware is addressed.

- Develop a process to determine if unauthorized or rogue hardware exist on the network and to address rogue hardware assets on a periodic basis.

- Develop or update awareness training to address the topic of rogue hardware.

- Conduct awareness training.

- Evaluate the effectiveness of the awareness training with respect to connecting rogue hardware to the network, and revise as needed.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization counsels all users who attempt to install rogue or unauthorized hardware to the organization’s networks.

Tier: Advanced.

CIS Controls Version 8 : The CIS Controls are a prioritized set of Safeguards to mitigate the most prevalent cyber-attacks against systems and networks. They are mapped to and referenced by multiple legal, regulatory, and policy frameworks.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations : This publication provides a catalog of security and privacy controls for information systems and organizations to protect organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation from a diverse set of threats and risks, including hostile attacks, human errors, natural disasters, structural failures, foreign intelligence entities, and privacy risks. AT-3

NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide: This publication assists organizations in establishing computer security incident response capabilities and handling incidents efficiently and effectively. This publication provides guidelines for incident handling, particularly for analyzing incident-related data and determining the appropriate response to each incident. The guidelines can be followed independently of particular hardware platforms, operating systems, protocols, or applications.

Family: Ransomware Readiness Assessment > User and Access Management (UM).

Source: CISA RRA, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are asset descriptions updated when changes to assets occur?
description:
WI:AM-1.Q4: Are asset descriptions updated when changes to assets occur?

Guidance: Importance: When changes to assets occur, asset descriptions should be updated to ensure that current protection and sustainment strategies continue to be satisfied.

Question Intent: To determine if asset descriptions are updated when changes to assets occur.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- When changes to assets occur, asset descriptions are updated for all changed assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- When changes to assets occur, asset descriptions are updated for some changed assets.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

- Asset description change documentation, asset inventory status, updated asset and service resilience requirements, updated asset and service protection strategies and controls, updated strategies and continuity plans for sustaining assets and services

Reference to standards/source assessments

- CRR: AM:G4.Q2-PITF

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-8, CM-8(1), PM-5

Tier: Basic.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CM-8; SP 800-53 R5 CM-8(1); SP 800-53 R5 PM-5.

Family: Withstand > Asset Management > Physical devices and systems within the organization are inventoried.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Is the baseline of network operations managed (reviewed and updated regularly)?
description:
WI:AE-1.Q2: Is the baseline of network operations managed (reviewed and updated regularly)?

Guidance: Importance: System information exchanges include connections via leased lines or virtual private networks, connections to internet service providers, database sharing or exchanges of database transaction information, connections and exchanges with cloud services, exchanges via web-based services, or exchanges of files via file transfer protocols, network protocols (e.g., IPv4, IPv6), email, or other organization-to-organization communications. Organizations consider the risk related to new or increased threats that may be introduced when systems exchange information with other systems that may have different security and privacy requirements and controls.

Question Intent: To determine if the established baseline of network operations is managed for all systems and assets that support the critical service.

- Baseline configurations are formally reviewed.

- Maintaining baseline configurations requires creating new baselines as organizational information systems change over time.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The established baseline of network operations is managed for all systems and assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The established baseline of network operations is managed for some systems and assets

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

- Change management documentation

- Security system review minutes or action items

- Network documentation change logs

- Dashboard of network monitoring solution

- SIEM solution management console

- Cloud service management console

- Firewall logs or console

Reference to standards/source assessments

- CERT RMM TM:SG4.SP2

- CRR: CCM:G3.Q4.

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CM-2

Tier: Advanced.

References: SP 800-53 R5 CM-2.

Family: Withstand > Anomalies and Events > A baseline of network operations and expected data flows for users and systems is established and managed.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Have physical and information security personnel been trained in their specific roles and responsibilities in support of the critical service?
description:
TA:G2.Q7: Have physical and information security personnel been trained in their specific roles and responsibilities in support of the critical service?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if physical and information security personnel have been trained in their specific roles and responsibilities.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AT-3, PM-13:

- Role-based security training is provided to physical and information security personnel with assigned security roles and responsibilities:

- before authorizing their access to the information system or before they perform their assigned duties

- when required by information system changes

- periodically (frequency defined by the organization) thereafter

- Comprehensive role-based training addresses management, operational, and technical roles and responsibilities.

- Role-based security training also applies to contractors providing services.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- All physical and information security personnel that support the critical service have been trained in their specific roles and responsibilities.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- Some physical and information security personnel have been trained in their specific roles and responsibilities.

References: Application Service Providers Standard; SP 800-53 R5 AT-3; SP 800-53 R5 PM-13; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 PR.AT-5.

CERT-RMM Reference
[OTA:SG4.SP1] Conduct training for physical and information security personnel. The organization must perform training to ensure staff are appropriately skilled in their roles. Experienced instructors should perform training. When possible, training is conducted in settings that closely resemble actual performance conditions and includes activities to simulate actual work situations. This approach includes integration of tools, methods, and procedures for competency development. Training is tied to work responsibilities so that on-the-job activities or other outside experiences will reinforce the training within a reasonable time after the training is completed.

Family: Training and Awareness (TA) > Goal 2 - Awareness and training activities are conducted..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are vulnerabilities analyzed to determine relevance to the organization? (Facilities)
description:
VM:G2.Q5: Are vulnerabilities analyzed to determine relevance to the organization?

VM:G2.Q5-F: Facilities

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if vulnerabilities are analyzed to determine relevance to the organization.
- Through vulnerability analysis, the organization seeks to understand the potential threat that the vulnerability represents.

- The organization should assign a course of action to each vulnerability based upon its relevance to the organization.
Vulnerability analysis includes activities to:
- understand the threat and exposure

- review trend information to determine whether the vulnerability existed before and what actions were taken to reduce or eliminate it

- identify and understand underlying causes for exposure to the vulnerability
Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization analyzes all vulnerabilities to determine their relevance to the critical service.
Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- The organization analyzes some vulnerabilities to determine their relevance to the critical service.

Family: Vulnerability Management (VM) > Goal 2 - A process for identifying and analyzing vulnerabilities is established and maintained..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Are the assets that directly support the critical service inventoried (technology includes hardware, software, and external information systems)?
description:
AM:G2.Q1: Are the assets that directly support the critical service inventoried (technology includes hardware, software, and external information systems)?

Guidance: Question Intent:

To determine if the assets that support the critical service are inventoried.

- The organization should inventory the assets (people, information, technology, and facilities) required for the delivery of the critical service.

- Inventories of assets may exist in multiple forms or physical locations.

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

- The organization inventories all assets that support the critical service.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

- The organization inventories some assets.

References: SP 800-18 R1; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM-1; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM-2; Cybersecurity Framework V1.1 ID.AM-4.

CERT-RMM Reference [ADM:SG1.SP1] Identify and inventory high-value assets. An organization must be able to identify its high-value assets, document them, and establish their value in order to develop strategies for protecting and sustaining assets commensurate with their value to services.

Family: Asset Management (AM) > Goal 2 - Assets are inventoried, and the authority and responsibility for these assets is established..

Source: CISA CRR, via CISA CSET v13.

name: Is access to the audit log repository restricted to those with a business need?
description:
WI:AE-3.Q5: Is access to the audit log repository restricted to those with a business need?

Guidance: Importance: It is imperative that only trusted subjects are only given the minimum privileges necessary for satisfying organizational mission/business needs relative to the organizations policy. This is most applicable when there is a mandate that establishes a policy regarding access to controlled unclassified information or classified information and some users of the system/repository are not authorized access to all such information resident in the system/repository.

Question Intent: To determine if there are restrictions to the audit log repositories based on mission/business need.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- There exists policy and controls that restrict access to systems/repositories based on business need.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- There exists policy and controls that restricts access to systems/repositories, but they are not based on business need.

Possible evidence

- Access enforcement policy

- List of users and what systems they have access to

- List of all user account types and holders

- Example of denying access due to account restrictions

Reference to standards/source assessments

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: AU-6, CA-7, IR-4, IR-5, IR-8, SI-4

Tier: Intermediate.

Family: Withstand > Anomalies and Events > Event data are collected and correlated from multiple sources and sensors.

Source: CISA MVRA (draft), via CISA CSET v13.

name: Does the organization back up data per the RTO and RPO requirements?
description:
WI:IP-4.Q4: Does the organization back up data per the RTO and RPO requirements?

Guidance: Importance: Organizations must not only establish RTOs and RPOs, but also implement backup solutions that meet those requirements (or adjust the requirements).

Question Intent: Whether the organization’s backup solution meets defined RTO and RPO requirements.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- The organization has a backup solution that meets organizationally defined RTO and RPO requirements

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The organization has a backup solution that meets the organizationally defined RTO or RPO.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

Possible evidence

- Documentation that show the backup solution meeting a defined RTO or RPO

Reference to standards/source assessments

- NIST 800-53, Rev. 5: CP-4, CP-6(2), CP-9

name: Is there adequate funding to perform risk management activities as planned?
description:
AN:GV-4.Q7: Is there adequate funding to perform risk management activities as planned?

Guidance: Importance: Funding is an indication of higher-level management support and sponsorship of risk management activities.

Question Intent: This question determines if adequate funding has been provided for risk management activities. The intent of the question is to evaluate the completeness of the funding, not the completeness of the plan.

Funding should be available to support the proper oversight, execution, and maintenance of risk management activities.

Considerations for funding planned risk management activities include:

- defining funding needs

- establishing a budget

- resolving funding gaps

- funding the process activities, including staffing, tools, training, etc.

Criteria for Full Implementation Response

- This must be true to mark a Yes.

Criteria for Partial Implementation Response

- The planned activities have only been partially funded.

- (Otherwise, the answer is marked as No Implementation)

- Attestation from stakeholders regarding funding for risk management activities.

name: Are resilience requirements evaluated as a result of changes to assets? (Information)
description:
CCM:G1.Q2: Are resilience requirements evaluated as a result of changes to assets?

CCM:G1.Q2-I: Information

Guidance: Question Intent:
To determine if resilience requirements are evaluated as a result of changes to assets.

- The organization should evaluate the impact of asset changes on existing resilience requirements.

- The requirements from all the services supported by the changed asset should be considered. Evaluating resilience requirements is especially critical when assets are shared between services.

Typical work products:

-   documented criteria that establishes when a change in requirements must be evaluated

-   requirements change history with rationale for performing the change

-   requirements baseline

-   resilience requirements included in change requests

-   updated asset resilience requirements

Criteria for “Yes” Response:

-   The organization evaluates all of the resilience requirements of each asset that supports the critical service when changes to the asset occur.

Criteria for “Incomplete” Response:

-   The organization evaluates some of the resilience requirements of each asset that supports the critical service when changes to the asset occur.

-   Or; The organization evaluates all of the resilience requirements of some assets when changes to the asset occur.

CERT-RMM Reference
[RRM:SG1.SP3] Evaluate the impact of requirement changes on existing activities and commitments for protecting and sustaining assets and services. The organization must independently monitor that the change management process is operational and that asset-level resilience requirements have been updated on a regular basis so that they remain in direct alignment with organizational drivers.
Additional References:

- NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CM-3

- NIST CSF References: PR.IP-3
